newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farmers blast gene maize production ban.
newsitem.headline: French farmers blast gene maize production ban.

text.p: French farmers reacted angrily on Thursday to an "incomprehensible" government decision to prevent them growing genetically modified maize even after allowing it to be imported from the United States.
Wednesday's cabinet decision would punish French farmers while failing to allay consumers' worries over the maize which was approved for import last week, farm union FNSEA said.
"The government's decision is incoherent and creates competitive distortions between farmers in France and other countries," France's leading farm union said in a statement.

Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur announced the planting ban on Wednesday, saying the government wanted to move step by step on an issue that has sparked protests from environmentalists and some consumer groups who say genetic techniques are a hazard.
"At this stage we must proceed with caution....we will not authorise the cultivation of gene-modified varieties this year," Vasseur told a news conference.

France adopted a European Union plan to allow imports of the maize last week, subject to labelling conditions. Because of the difficulty of segregating the maize, labels will say that food products concerned "may contain gene-modified materials".
But that has further infuriated the FNSEA which says the wording is not strong enough to dispel consumer doubts and will merely confuse the marketing of such crops even further.
French farmers, some of whom helped test the maize on behalf of Swiss inventor Ciba-Ceigy, had hoped for approval to grow it commercially in time for their next sowings in April.
Because the new strand is designed to resist the corn borer pest, which often results in part of the maize crop being lost, its use would have reduced the cost of buying insecticides.
Farmers say they have to use expensive air-spraying to fight the borer which attacks maize when the plants are tall.
Environmental group Greenpeace, which has led protests against the maize being introduced to Europe, welcomed the government's decision to prevent it being grown locally.
"It was high time France showed its determination not to accept cultivation of genetic maize," it said on Wednesday.
But it said the government should now go further and reverse its decision to allow the maize to be imported at all.
Maize is used mainly for feeding animals as well as starch production and appears as an ingredient in many processed foods.
France produced around 14 million tonnes of maize in 1996.

Backed by the United States, which started growing the variety last year, Swiss Ciba-Geigy says its so-called Bt-maize is safe and that it will seek to address any popular resistance to its product through open information.
